name: Thoracic Oncology, Anatomic Lobectomy, and Pleural Empyema
hyTerms: gold standard for stage I-II NSCLC
chest computed tomography with IV contrast

reference.source: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed / Shields General Thoracic Surgery 8th ed
clinicalPearls: Anatomic lobectomy with systematic mediastinal lymph node dissection is gold standard for stage I-II NSCLC
Preoperative predicted postoperative FEV1 and DLCO > 40% confirm safe physiological pulmonary reserve
Spontaneous pneumothorax with persistent air leak > 3 days or second episode warrants VATS blebectomy & pleurodesis
Pleural empyema progresses from exudative to fibrinopurulent to organizing trapped lung requiring decortication
Anterior mediastinal masses follow the 4 Ts: Thymoma, Teratoma, Thyroid substernal, and Terrible lymphoma
reference.pathophysiology: Lung carcinomas develop through multistep bronchial epithelial mutagenic alterations driven by tobacco carcinogens and oncogenes (EGFR, KRAS, ALK). Pleural empyema arises from parapneumonic bacterial translocation across the visceral pleura, initiating intense neutrophil influx, fibrin deposition, and intrapleural loculations that consolidate into a rigid collagenous peel trapping the lung.
additionalDifferentials: Benign granulomatous solitary pulmonary nodule (tuberculoma, histoplasmosis)
Tension pneumothorax vs massive pulmonary embolism
Parapneumonic sterile effusion vs complicated empyema thoracis
additionalInvestigations: High-resolution chest computed tomography with IV contrast
Whole-body 18F-FDG PET-CT and endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) nodal staging
Pulmonary function tests with spirometry, DLCO, and arterial blood gas
Diagnostic thoracentesis with pleural fluid pH, glucose, LDH, Gram stain, and culture
